name: The Secret: Dead Man's Switch design
goalName: Design a game for an object with set mechanics
goal:
My team is given a device with mechanics that are not allowed to change. A game must be made where this device plays a role in. The game's purpose is to pass a bit of time while waiting for the bus.
The device:<<image The Secret - Device.png>>The device has the following components:
- 1 button
- X switches / toggles
- 1 indicator light

The mechanics of the device are as follows:
- When the button is pressed, the sequence of the switch states is saved.
- When the sequence is later reproduced, the indicator lights up. Otherwise nothing happens.

approach.text: Me and my group started by brainstorming, as this is the fastest way to come up with the most potential ideas for games. I came up with the idea of a game with a bomb, where 1 of the switches is a switch that sets off the bomb. The players have to try a switch one by one, until someone toggles the bomb switch. The survivors are the winners.
When the idea was made, we compared it to other games. A team member thought of Russian Roulette. I thought of the minigame Bowser's Big Blast from Mario Party.

The game's tension is the main mood of the game, but the players have to be engaged to achieve enthusiastic gameplay. To get the players engaged, the team decided to create stories for the games, which is covered in a different devlog.

When the game's design was ready, me and teammates tried the game out on testers. All players indicated that 8 was a good amount of switches on the device. This worked out great, as another game required the amount of switches to be a multiple of 4. The feedback was positive, though there was a bit of confusion about the win-state of the game.
There were two assumptions:
1. The game is won when all but 1 switches are tried out (so every switch except the bomb). Then all players win.
2. The last switch must be toggled. The person to toggle this switch knows that this is the bomb and has to accept defeat.

Unfortunately, there was no time left to test which win-state was more enjoyable. This would have been a great opportunity for A/B testing.

normalLearnings: I know how to create games with predefined, immutable rules.
I learned to think more about the win-state of games, achieved by playtesting or roleplaying when designing.
result: Dead Man's Switch can be played with 3 to 9 people. The game is quick and easy to understand for all test subjects, making it suitable for the given scenario at the bus stop.
validation: The game has been tested, and approved by all testers. The only downside testers indicate is that there is no logical reason to have to turn the switches off when one is toggled on.
contribution: The designing of this game is a great refresher for the semester.
